title: [finding] The attribution footer is appended on the CREATE path too — a hand-written one lands doubled on every PR body and report comment, with no PATCH involved
body:
Filed **unassigned**, recording only, by the `os-dev` seat working objectstack#14663 (session `session_019RfFHiRCSs3JXLK4cwcfox`). Out of that card's scope — recorded rather than fixed. `finding` = awaiting first grading; `domain:*` and `type` left for triage.

## The measurement

The attribution footer is appended by the platform **on the create path**, to both an issue comment and a PR body. An artifact whose author also writes the footer — as `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` instructs — therefore lands with **two**, with no PATCH anywhere in the sequence.

Both artifacts today, each sent with exactly one hand-written footer, each read back immediately over REST:

| artifact | sent | stored | appended by the platform |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| issue comment 5528999279 on 14663 | 1769 B | 1827 B | `\n\n\n---\n_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_` (bare form) |
| PR 14995 body, at creation | 8324 B | 8415 B | `\n\n---\n_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_...)_` (session-URL form) |

In both cases the sent bytes are a **byte-identical prefix** of the stored bytes: nothing was rewritten, nothing was stripped, one block was appended. The appended form matches the recorded per-channel spelling — bare on the comment channel, session-URL on PR create — so the *form* half of the recorded rule holds exactly.

## Why it is worth recording

**It contradicts the create leg of a closed card's recorded pattern.** objectstack#11273 (closed) measured PATCH accretion and recorded the pattern as "**create → one footer**; each subsequent body edit → one more". The create leg no longer separates that cleanly: create appends one too, so the count at creation is one *plus whatever the author wrote*. Today that is two, before any edit exists to blame.

**The instruction and the mechanism now disagree.** `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` tells the dev to end a PR body with the session-URL footer and lists the two footer forms per channel. Read as an authoring instruction — which is how it reads — following it exactly produces the doubled footer on every governed PR and every report comment the fleet writes. Read as a *description of what the platform will append*, the clause is correct and the dev should write no footer at all. Nothing in the text picks between the two readings, and both are live in the fleet right now: this card's own dev read it the first way.

**The cost is small, recurring, and lands in the artifact humans review.** A doubled footer on every dev PR body and every report comment, and — per the closed card — a normalisation loop (1 → 2 → 3) for any agent that tries to clean it up by editing.

## What this is NOT

⛔ Not a claim that anything is stripped: the sent bytes survive verbatim in both artifacts. ⛔ Not the PATCH behaviour of the closed card — no PATCH was issued here. ⛔ Not a proposal to edit the contract: `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` is a governed protocol surface and was explicitly out of this dev's file surface, so the site is reported, not touched.

## What a resolution would need to decide

1. Whether the os-dev footer clause is an **authoring instruction** or a **description of an appended block** — and then say so in one word, since the two readings differ by exactly "write it" versus "do not write it".
2. Whether the closed card's recorded "create → one footer" line needs the correction above, wherever that reading now lives.

## Evidence

Read-backs are the REST `GET` of each artifact immediately after its `POST`, compared byte-wise against the file that was sent: `sent.startsWith` holds in both directions of the comparison used, and the whole difference is the appended block quoted in the table.
